title: 사진 조명 시각 의미 및 후보팩 강화 제안

observed_repository_baseline.provenance_limit: The visual-obligation source was already modified by other work. The 275-profile count and hashes remain a read-only research snapshot; the later implementation appended only the lighting profiles owned by this task and regenerated indexes without claiming unrelated concurrent changes.

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A relatively small acting source creates one coherent direction, crisp cast-shadow boundaries, short penumbrae, decisive form shadows, and localized specular response without requiring darkness or clipping.
component_groups: one coherent source direction links highlights form shadows and cast shadows
cast-shadow edges remain crisp with a short visible penumbra
shadow shapes correspond to the occluding subject or object geometry
specular highlights are comparatively compact and directionally owned
lit surfaces and shadow structure remain exposed rather than clipped or crushed

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A relatively large acting source keeps one readable direction while producing broad shadow-edge transitions, gradual form modeling, broad specular response, and open but still shaped shadows.
component_groups: one readable source direction survives instead of becoming flat ambient wash
cast and form shadow edges cross a broad gradual transition
curved forms move progressively from light through midtone into shadow
specular response spreads broadly across compatible glossy surfaces
shadow detail remains open while contours and volume stay legible

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: An elevated off-axis key creates a short nose shadow that falls down and slightly sideways but remains visibly separated from the cheek shadow, preserving modeled cheeks and a readable far eye.
component_groups: one elevated off-axis key owns the face lighting
the nose shadow falls downward and slightly toward the shadow side
the nose shadow remains clearly separated from the cheek shadow mass
both cheeks retain modeled light-to-shadow structure and the far eye remains readable
the geometry excludes a Rembrandt triangle split midline and centered butterfly shadow

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A high near-frontal key creates a compact centered shadow directly beneath the nose with largely symmetrical cheek illumination and upper catchlights, without the lower-return evidence that defines clamshell light.
component_groups: one dominant key sits high and close to the camera axis
a compact shadow falls directly beneath the nose near the facial centerline
left and right cheek illumination remains broadly symmetrical
upper catchlights and gentle cheek-jaw modeling remain visible
the dominant upper single-key geometry remains distinct from lower-return or high-low catchlight-pair patterns

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A near-side key produces a clear face-center division so one half is illuminated and the other half remains modeled shadow, while the head contour and shadow-side structure stay readable enough to distinguish the pattern from silhouette.
component_groups: one side key approaches a lateral ninety-degree relation to the face
the principal light-shadow boundary tracks the nose and face center region
one face half is decisively illuminated while the other is decisively shadowed
the shadow half preserves eye contour cheek and jaw structure
the face remains a two-sided modeled subject rather than a solid silhouette or broad-light turn

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A turned face presents one visibly broader cheek plane to the camera and that broader visible plane receives the dominant light, while the narrower far plane carries the primary shadow.
component_groups: the head turn makes one cheek plane visibly broader to the camera
the camera-broad cheek plane receives the dominant key illumination
the narrower far plane carries the primary modeled shadow
nose cheek eye and jaw cues preserve both face orientation and light ownership
the relation is defined by camera-facing area rather than fixed left or right side

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A turned face presents one narrow far cheek plane to the camera and that narrow plane receives the dominant light, leaving the broader camera-facing cheek in modeled shadow.
component_groups: the head turn makes one cheek plane narrow and the opposite cheek broad to the camera
the camera-narrow cheek plane receives the dominant key illumination
the broad near cheek carries the primary modeled shadow
face contour eye line and nose direction remain readable through the shadow
the relation is defined by camera-facing area rather than fixed left or right side

activation_terms: key fill separation background lighting roles
키 필 분리 배경광 역할 관계
proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A primary key models the subject, a subordinate fill opens the key-owned shadows without a second opposing shadow, a rear or side edge separates the subject, and background illumination supports rather than erases that hierarchy.
component_groups: one primary key direction owns the subject form and principal shadow
a weaker broad fill opens that same shadow without creating an opposing double shadow
a controlled rear or side edge separates at least one subject contour from the background
background light supplies texture color or directional support without flattening the subject
the four roles remain hierarchically distinct rather than becoming even omnidirectional illumination

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A rear or rear-side source creates a narrow coherent luminous contour along selected subject edges while front or side modeling remains readable and the contour visibly separates the subject from the background.
component_groups: a rear or rear-side source direction is consistent across illuminated edges
a narrow rim follows actual hair shoulder object or material contours
the front or side of the subject retains readable form and detail
the bright edge creates local separation from a darker or similar-toned background
the contour remains selective and plausible rather than a uniform cutout halo

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A bright field behind the subject leaves the subject as a predominantly dark connected mass whose outer contour and pose are immediately readable while internal front detail is intentionally minimal.
component_groups: a bright background or source field clearly sits behind the subject
the subject reads as one predominantly dark connected mass
the outer contour pose and major negative spaces remain immediately legible
internal front-facing texture and facial detail stay intentionally minimal
a thin rim or merely dark exposure does not substitute for the mass-background relation

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: Most of the frame occupies light tonal regions with open shallow shadows, preserved white and highlight detail, a low-to-moderate key-fill difference, and enough edge or color separation to keep the subject distinct.
component_groups: light tones occupy most of the frame without erasing the principal subject
shadows remain shallow open and visibly shaped rather than absent
white surfaces and bright highlights preserve texture below clipping
key and fill differ modestly while one modeling direction remains readable
subject edges stay separated by contour tone or color within the bright field

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: Dark tonal regions dominate, but selected subject planes receive deliberate readable illumination, shadow structure remains differentiated, highlights retain detail, and the frame hierarchy cannot be explained by global underexposure.
component_groups: dark tonal regions dominate the frame by deliberate spatial design
selected face object or material planes receive coherent directional light
shadow regions retain more than one density and preserve structural clues
small highlights remain controlled and detailed rather than clipped
correctly exposed lit regions prove selective illumination rather than global underexposure

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: Directional light and connected shadow masses model three-dimensional volume through diffused values, specular accents, form shadows, and transitional midtones, making contrast serve shape rather than darkness alone.
component_groups: one dominant direction organizes illuminated and shadowed planes
light-dark boundaries follow three-dimensional face object or drapery form
diffuse value specular accent and form shadow remain distinguishable
midtone transitions connect selected highlights to deep but structured shadows
the composition uses alternating light and dark masses to guide form and attention

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A predominantly dark field contains one or a few abruptly isolated coherent pools of illumination whose protected local detail and sparse peripheral clues create a concentrated hierarchy more extreme than ordinary low-key light.
component_groups: a continuous dark field dominates the background and much of the subject environment
one or a few coherent light pools isolate the principal action or form
light-to-dark transition is abrupt enough to create a concentrated hierarchy
the isolated lit area preserves color texture and highlight detail
sparse peripheral clues maintain spatial context without filling the dark field

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A small near-camera-axis flash makes the near subject abruptly bright with compact specular hotspots and a hard shadow close behind, while ambient distance falls darker or remains separately exposed.
component_groups: the dominant flash direction stays close to the camera viewing axis
a crisp cast shadow falls close behind the near subject on available surfaces
skin glossy fabric or objects show compact frontal specular hotspots
the near subject is much brighter than a more distant ambient background
some ambient or spatial background evidence remains instead of a white clipped void

activation_terms: warm practical cool ambient ownership relation
proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A visible practical source owns a nearby pool whose direction and color continue onto the subject, while a distinct ambient zone remains spatially coherent and all major shadows can be assigned without contradiction.
component_groups: at least one plausible practical source is visible within the scene
a nearby brightness and color pool falls off outward from that source
light reaching the subject matches the practical's plausible direction and color family
a second ambient zone remains spatially distinct in color brightness or direction
cast and form shadows have coherent source ownership without teal-orange grade substitution

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A coherent source direction passes through or around identifiable occluders into a scattering medium, forming separated shafts that continue to visible receiving surfaces and shadow gaps.
component_groups: one coherent source direction anchors every visible shaft
a window cloud foliage architecture or gobo provides identifiable occlusion gaps
haze dust mist or atmosphere makes the light path visible within volume
separate bright shafts and darker gaps preserve the occluder's pattern
at least one shaft lands plausibly on a subject floor wall or atmospheric layer

activation_terms: low warm backlight with long shadow
proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A low horizon-side warm direct source creates long shadows and grazing or rim highlights while cooler or neutral open-sky fill preserves the shadow side; color alone does not establish the relation.
component_groups: the dominant direct source arrives from a visibly low horizon-side direction
cast shadows extend long across readable ground or architecture
warm grazing backlight or rim light traces selected contours and textures
cooler or neutral open-sky fill preserves readable shadow-side information
spatial direction and shadow length distinguish the look from a global warm grade

activation_terms: 차가운 황혼과 따뜻한 도시 조명 관계
proposed_hard_profiles.definition: Cool twilight sky ambient remains bright enough to reveal environment and subject contours while localized warm practical pools are visible and balanced, with no direct sun and no substitution by a cyan night grade.
component_groups: a cool twilight sky or open ambient field remains visibly luminous
cool twilight ambient and localized warm practicals own the scene instead of a direct sun disk or hard high-sun shadow
warm practical sources create localized pools on streets windows or subjects
ambient and practical exposure remain balanced so neither becomes a blank field
architecture and subject contours preserve cool-warm spatial separation

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A strong source near or inside the frame generates one or more secondary translucent ghost shapes whose positions, scale changes, and optical repetition align coherently with the source and lens axis.
component_groups: one strong source near or inside the frame anchors the optical effect
one or more secondary translucent ghost shapes are spatially displaced from the source
the ghost sequence follows a coherent source-to-frame-center or lens-axis alignment
ghost scale color and opacity vary as related internal-reflection images rather than random stickers
scene detail outside the ghost path remains distinct enough to separate ghosting from veiling haze

activation_terms: 베일링 플레어 국소 대비 저하 관계
proposed_hard_profiles.definition: A strong source near or inside the frame spreads a broad optical veil that lowers black density and local contrast more strongly toward the source while preserving a directional gradient across the scene.
component_groups: one bright source near or inside the frame plausibly drives the veil
a broad translucent haze spreads from the source-side region
black density and local edge contrast decrease within that region
the contrast loss follows a directional gradient instead of covering the frame uniformly
some unaffected reference region remains for comparison against fog or low-contrast grading

proposed_hard_profiles.definition: Very bright highlight boundaries carry a thin localized warm or red-biased halo just outside the exposed edge, while the highlight core and surrounding nonhighlight detail remain sufficiently structured to reject global glow and flare.
component_groups: one or more genuinely high-luminance edges anchor the effect
a thin warm or red-biased halo sits immediately outside those edges
halo width and intensity fall off locally rather than covering the frame
highlight core shape and adjacent nonhighlight detail remain readable
aligned ghost orbs broad veiling haze and chromatic edge pairs remain visibly distinct from the thin local halo

candidate_pack_policy.cluster_rule: Every cluster owns a primary tag and one candidate in each required slot. Individual entries may be omitted only when the requesting profile supplies the same owned relation; cross-cluster substitutions are not allowed.

candidate_or_metadata_only_terms.rule: Preserve explicit requester metadata and offer a bounded visible-effect translation, but never create a hard profile or infer the actual device, metric, or product from generated pixels.

postprocess_lane.rule: Postprocess candidates may combine with a lighting cluster, but they cannot satisfy or replace a scene-light component group. Process names must be labeled as looks unless the requester supplies capture or lab metadata.
